problem: End-to-end image-goal navigation policies that learn visual representations from scratch need large amounts of costly interaction data (about 60k samples) and suffer from domain shift between training and test environments.
motivation: Goal-image navigation mainly needs the relative 2D transformation between the current view and the goal view, which can be described as pan, tilt and zoom (PTZ). That transformation is independent of image statistics, so it can be pre-trained without any interaction data or target-domain images, which would cut the interaction data needed.
key_idea: Pre-train a fixed PTZ encoder by regressing the location and scale of a random crop between two views on synthetic noise images (Perlin, fractal, random shapes), then train only a small LSTM policy on the low-dimensional PTZ states with little interaction data.
insight: The PTZ relation between two views is largely independent of the underlying visual statistics, so an encoder trained on noise alone reaches 92.2% overlap IOU and 93.2% non-overlap accuracy on natural home images, versus 97.1% and 98.8% when trained on Habitat images. The ablations show that fractal noise is the best single noise source. They also show that a curriculum (overlapping crops first, non-overlapping crops added later) is essential: fractal without the curriculum gets only 2.7% non-overlap accuracy, and a policy using an encoder trained on Habitat images with overlapping crops only navigates worse than one using noise-trained PTZ with both crop types. Because PTZ is low-dimensional, a feed-forward policy on 2k interaction samples beats an end-to-end system trained on 60k, and longer LSTM sequences overfit in the low-data regime.
method: PTZ representation: the goal view is treated as a crop of the current view, and its pan, tilt and zoom factors (p,t,z) serve as a 3-DOF spatial state for local navigation.

PTZ encoder: a ResNet18 takes a concatenated pair of 128x128 crops from a 256x256 image and regresses (p,t,z). The goal crop has scale 0.5-1 and is resized back to 128x128; non-overlapping pairs are labeled (0,0,0).
Synthetic noise pre-training data: 40k noise images made of 10k Perlin, 10k fractal and 20k random-shape images, plus single-noise 40k variants. Training uses no action labels and no real images.
Curriculum: the encoder is trained first on overlapping crops until convergence, and non-overlapping crops are mixed in afterwards, because training both together converges slowly on noise.

Navigation policy: the PTZ encoder is frozen and a single-layer LSTM with 512 hidden units regresses actions from PTZ states with L1 loss, trained on random-exploration data (2k, 30k or 60k samples) from 10 Gibson scenes. Sub-trajectory length 1 makes it a feed-forward net.
Baseline end-to-end system: a generic encoder trained jointly with the LSTM on the same interaction data.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 PTZ encoder (frozen, pre-trained on noise) + single-layer LSTM policy (512 hidden)
setting.training_data: PTZ encoder: 40k synthetic noise images (Perlin/fractal/shapes), self-supervised. Policy: random-exploration interaction data of 2k/30k/60k samples from 10 Gibson scenes.
setting.observation: monocular RGB current view + goal image
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions (forward and turns), with an LSTM regressing the action; the task is local navigation with the goal in the same room
setting.privileged: none (a success check uses the GT goal location within 0.5 m plus perceptual similarity to the goal image, for evaluation only)

numbers_note: Navigation results are reported only in figures (Fig. 2 a/b) as success-rate curves, with no numeric values in the text. The tables give PTZ encoder accuracy only, not navigation benchmark metrics. The task is a custom local Gibson image-goal task, not a canonical benchmark.
results: On the PTZ evaluation over 2300 home images, the all-noise encoder scores 92.2% overlap IOU and 93.2% non-overlap accuracy, close to the Habitat-trained 97.1% and 98.8%. In navigation, a PTZ-enabled policy with 2k interaction samples and sequence length 1 outperforms the best end-to-end policy trained on 60k samples. Fractal noise alone is nearly as good as all noises combined.
limitations: Evaluated only on short-range local navigation, with the goal in the same room and five forward steps away, in simulated Gibson scenes with no real robot.
Navigation results are given only as plots without numeric tables, and the setup is small: 5 test scenes and 30 episodes each.
The 3-DOF PTZ state assumes the goal is visible as a crop of the current view, so it does not cover long-horizon or map-based navigation.
